https://www.ibtimes.com/short-sellers-ke.text: Elon Musk is saying that those short-selling SpaceX stock will get burned. Responding to a social media publication noting the percentage of company shares being used for that purpose, he said: "I try to warn them, but they just double down."The company is facing a pivotal moment later on Tuesday as it is set to deliver its first earnings call.The company, which debuted on Wall Street in June at $135 per share, quickly became one of the hottest stocks of the year before losing a little less than half its value from its peak. Investors are now hoping the earnings report will provide evidence that SpaceX can justify its lofty valuation and reignite confidence after the stock's steep decline.Shares closed Monday at $114.53, down 15% from the initial public offering price and nearly 49% below the record high of $225 reached just days after trading began. It was climbing close to 10% on Tuesday at 3:12 p.m. ET. The selloff has erased more than $1 trillion in market value from its peak, making the company's first earnings release one of the most closely watched events of the corporate season.But despite the hype, analysts warn that the results themselves may not offer the clarity investors are seeking. Unlike mature technology companies, SpaceX remains unprofitable and continues to invest heavily in ambitious long-term projects spanning satellite internet, reusable rockets, artificial intelligence and future orbital infrastructure."There is so much that's in the future of the SpaceX story," Drew Cupps, portfolio manager and head of the 5Perspectives Growth Team at Polen Capital, told Bloomberg. "There's not a lot of here and now."Wall Street expects SpaceX to report a second quarter loss of 24 cents per share on revenue of approximately $6.8 billion. However, those forecasts have become increasingly uncertain as analysts struggle to model a company with limited public financial history.Bloomberg reported that consensus estimates for the company's quarterly loss have widened by about 18% over the past month, underscoring the uncertainty surrounding the business.Instead of focusing solely on the quarterly numbers, analysts say management's outlook may carry even greater weight. Investors are expected to closely scrutinize updates on the company's Starlink satellite network, commercial launch business and artificial intelligence initiatives, all of which are viewed as key drivers of SpaceX's long-term growth strategy.The earnings report also comes at a particularly delicate time because a major share lockup expiration is just around the corner.On Aug. 6, roughly 911.5 million shares valued at more than $100 billion will become eligible for sale as restrictions on early investors expire. Bloomberg noted that billions of additional shares are scheduled to be unlocked later this year, creating the possibility of increased selling pressure and greater stock volatility.

https://www.politico.eu/article/latvian-.text: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs’ United List has won the country’s parliamentary election by a wide margin, putting the pro-Ukraine leader in a strong position to remain in power. With almost all votes counted following Saturday’s election, the center-right United List won around 35% of the vote — more than 20 percentage points ahead of the far-right Latvia First party, led by veteran politician Ainārs Šlesers, who opposes restrictive tariffs on Russia. Preliminary results released on Sunday put United List on course for 42 of the 100 seats in the national parliament. Advertisement Advertisement Despite the decisive victory — far stronger than pre-election polling suggested — Kulbergs will still need to negotiate with other parties to form a majority government. Two partners in his outgoing coalition, the conservative National Alliance and center-right New Unity, cleared the 5% threshold and are set to return to parliament. They appear to have enough seats for a majority without the Union of Greens and Farmers, which fell below the threshold. That gives Kulbergs a solid path to another pro-Ukraine coalition without having to seek support from Šlesers’ Latvia First, an option that had loomed over the election campaign, which was marked by high inflation, uncertainty around the troubled national airline airBaltic and instrumentalized migration orchestrated by Russia and Belarus. Kulbergs became prime minister in late May after his predecessor, Evika Siliņa, stood down following a backlash over stray Ukrainian drone strikes . The final stretch of Latvia’s election campaign also spilled into Brussels last week, where Kulbergs initially opposed an EU deal to remove Russian billionaires Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman from the bloc’s sanctions list. Latvia ultimately abstained , allowing the broader sanctions regime to be extended after a compromise among EU countries. Advertisement Advertisement

https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/11/us-s.text: A 41-year-old American soldier has been arrested near Gloucester on suspicion of spying for Russia, in an operation British counter-terrorism police carried out with help from US military and law enforcement agencies.The serviceman was detained on Tuesday under national security legislation and taken to a police station in London, where he remains in custody, the Metropolitan Police said.“This significant arrest and investigation is a result of close collaboration between UK and US authorities,” said Vicki Evans, Senior National Coordinator for Counter Terrorism Policing.“The allegations are serious and our investigation is very much ongoing,” Evans added.Officers said the case was “not linked to any other ongoing Counter Terrorism Policing investigations.”FBI director Kash Patel thanked British police and intelligence services for their work on the case.“This important arrest involves allegations of espionage, which is of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies,” Patel said in the police statement.Sean Stinchon, commanding general of US Army Counterintelligence Command, said the alleged conduct of a “senior soldier, entrusted with sensitive information” was a “sobering reminder that insider threats are real and persistent”.The Pentagon referred questions to the US Army, which did not immediately respond to requests for more details.The arrest is the latest in a series of espionage cases in the UK linked to Moscow. Britain has been one of Kyiv’s strongest backers since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.In September, a British man appeared in court in London accused of preparing to sabotage drone manufacturing sites for Russian military intelligence.Relations between London and Moscow were strained well before the war. In 2006, former Russian spy Alexander Litvinenko was poisoned in London, and in 2018 there was an attempt to poison double agent Sergei Skripal in Salisbury.
